main_text.p: aliquem expetunt, quasi proprium receptaculum, adeoq; domicilium in quo conserventur.

Tertium, à signo siue à communi loquendi con-§suetudine: Veteres posuerunt vacuum, in quod corpora reciperentur, idq; locum etiam appellarunt, dicentes, locum esse vacuum, ubi nullum corpus continetur, sed contineri posset. Ergo vel hic receptus loquendi mos testatur locum esse. Dicimus autem, rationem hanc sumptam à loquendi consuetudine, quòd vacuum revera in natura dari nullum potest: loquendi tamen consuetudo obtinuit, ut vacuum nominetur, in quo nullum corpus sensibus expositum apparet.

Quartum, à pronunciato Hesiodi in 1. Theogo-4nias. Is enim constituit ante res conditas quoddam chaos, commune omnium earum quæ post conditæ sunt rerum receptaculum, adeoq; locum. Igitur locus est, quodq; ad dignitatem eius facit, etiam ante alias res naturales, utpote quæ subsistere non potuissent, si non fuisset prius quidam locus, in quo colligerentur. Hæc argumenta ad stabiliendum partem affirmatiuam certa ac valida sunt.

page.notes: The right-margin marks after "con-" (paragraph 2) and after "Theogo-" are section marks, transcribed as printed; the first is uncertain (§ [?]). The mark beside "necessariò" is read as "1." but may be "2." The word at the bottom right is "cus" followed by a flourish, probably an abbreviation mark, which is not transcribed. Printed spelling is kept, including "conserventur" and "Hesiodi"; "uacuum" and similar forms are normalised to u/v convention. The long s is rendered as plain s throughout.
